articles.title: Jason Kelce private jet: Inside the $12 million Swiss designed Pilatus aircraft reportedly associated with the NFL broadcaster
articles.summary: Jason Kelce spent 13 successful seasons in the NFL, amassing $81 million in total career earnings.
articles.body: Jason Kelce spent 13 successful seasons in the NFL, amassing $81 million in total career earnings. The former Philadelphia Eagles center’s estimated net worth in 2026 is $60 million, as per Celebrity Net Worth. The ESPN studio analyst continues to build his off-gridiron profile through broadcasting, endorsements, and podcasting.Among his luxury assets, the retired NFL star reportedly owns a $12 million private jet: a Swiss-designed 2021 model Pilatus PC-24 Super Versatile Jet, according to AeroCorner. The aircraft has nine seats, two Williams FJ44-series engines, and weighs less than 12,500 pounds, according to FlightAware.Jason Kelce’s reported private jet detailsJason Kelce’s reported private jet, Pilatus PC-24, bears registration number N620JK. “62” was Jason’s jersey number in Philadelphia. And JK could be short for “Jason Kelce.”The aircraft is registered under Kelce Air LLC, a Delaware-based limited liability company, as per FlightAware’s aircraft registration database. The registration identifies Kelce Air LLC as the owner; aviation reports like AeroCorner associate the aircraft with Travis Kelce’s brother, Jason Kelce.According to AeroCorner’s recent report, the private jet associated with the NFL broadcaster is a 2021-manufactured Pilatus PC-24. The aircraft’s registration certificate was issued in November 2024, while its airworthiness date is in December 2024. Its registry source is FAA. FlightAware also lists the same exact details.The Philadelphia Eagles star’s supposed aircraft is classified as a fixed-wing, multi-engine airplane. Its assigned registration date is November 2024, while its expiration date is November 2031, which is seven years from its registration. The registered owner is listed as Kelce Air LLC. And the listed address is New Castle, Delaware.As per StarStyleHomes, Jason Kelce lives in Haverford, Pennsylvania, a township in Delaware County on the edge of Philadelphia’s Main Line. That’s the Delaware connection. According to AeroCorner, the aircraft is based in Wilmington, Delaware, just 10 minutes from Philadelphia International. AeroCorner estimates the aircraft at $12.2 million.Pilatus PC 24 jet specifications and performanceSwiss aircraft company Pilatus manufactures the PC-24. It is called a Super Versatile Jet because it has a dual role: business-aviation comfort and short-runway performance.Two William FJ44-series turbofan engines power the jet. It has a thrust rating of 3433 pounds. Its takeoff distance is 3,090 ft. The PC-24’s maximum speed is 440 knots and a maximum range of 2,000 nautical miles with six passengers. It can operate from unpaved runways, including grass, gravel, earth, paved strips, and snow-covered surfaces.Its landing gear and design let it access smaller airports unsuitable for larger business jets. Inside, it boasts a spacious cabin, flat floor, and a large cargo door. It’s ideal for business travel and journeys that involve carrying extra baggage.Jason Kelce private jet and NFL travel lifestyleIn February 2024, after Super Bowl LVIII in Las Vegas, Jason Kelce was spotted leaving Harry Reid International Airport through the commercial terminal. Barstool Sports reported that Kelce chose commercial travel even though most wealthy attendees at the Las Vegas championship game preferred to fly via private aircrafts.He earned widespread praise from fans as a “man of the people.” The report noted that over 500 private jets had left the city, but Jason was photographed flying commercially. The commercial flight travel took place reportedly before the Pilatus PC-24 registration date.The reported super versatile jet was registered in November 2024. The Pilatus PC-24 is owned by “KELCE AIR LLC.”An article published by Tim de Vries of AeroCorner also points out that the only Kelce brother associated with an aircraft registered through Kelce Air LLC is Jason. Travis Kelce reportedly doesn’t own an aircraft, he charters and flies as a passenger, as per AeroCorner.Or maybe this N620JK belongs to all the Kelces. But if it were Travis’, then wouldn’t it be N870TK? Just speculating. His billionaire pop superstar wife, Taylor Swift, owns a reported $54 million Dassault Falcon 7X private jet registered as N621MM. Maybe he doesn’t need one. So the Pilates aircraft could be Jason’s. articles.summary: In July, Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce received a special message that put the spotlight on a meaningful part of their wedding celebrations.
articles.body: In July, Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce received a special message that put the spotlight on a meaningful part of their wedding celebrations. Before getting married, the couple reportedly donated $26 million to charitable organisations across the United States. Among the beneficiaries was New York Cares, which recently shared a touching Instagram post expressing its gratitude. The organisation's message was more than a simple thank-you. It recognised how the couple had used an important milestone in their relationship to support people facing difficult circumstances, turning their pre-wedding generosity into something that could make a lasting difference.New York Cares shares emotional message for Taylor Swift and Travis KelceThe organisation shared a purple-themed appreciation card addressed directly to the newlyweds. Its message included a sweet reference to Swift's music, making the acknowledgement particularly special for the singer's fans.“Dear Taylor and Travis,We’re Enchanted to receive your generous gift to support New Yorkers in need.Thank you for making our mission a part of your Love Story.Best wishes,new york cares.”Alongside the graphic, New York Cares explained how the contribution would help strengthen its work across New York City. The organisation highlighted its efforts to address food insecurity, provide winter clothing and support children through essential resources.Its achievements include more than 70 million meals served, over eight million volunteer hours, 2.7 million winter coats distributed, more than 720,000 Winter Wishes granted to children and over 70,000 backpacks provided to students.For those unfamiliar with the organisation, New York Cares is a nonprofit that connects volunteers with community programmes across New York City. Its work focuses on supporting underserved communities through food distribution, education, winter assistance and other essential services.The organisation also encouraged Swift's supporters to take part in its charitable efforts, writing, "And to the Swifties who want to celebrate with us, we'd love to start your Giving Era."Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's $26 million donation supports charitiesNew York Cares was among more than a dozen organisations that publicly acknowledged the couple's pre-wedding contribution. Their reported $26 million donation reached charities in several cities with personal connections to Swift and Kelce, including Reading, Pennsylvania, Cleveland, Nashville and Kansas City.The Grammy Museum Foundation also thanked the couple for their "transformative gift", explaining that the contribution would help expand music education opportunities for students across the country.Kansas City's Harvesters food bank shared its own message of appreciation, writing, “We’d like to send a heartfelt thank you to @taylorswift and @killatrav for their very generous donation to our food bank just prior to their big wedding day. The two of them have incredibly big hearts and have shown up to support not only us but many charities over the years. We feel so lucky that they make the conscious effort to invest in hunger relief and the beautiful community we call Kansas City!”Dolly Parton also joined the list of well-wishers, thanking Swift and Kelce for their $2 million donation to her Imagination Library, which provides free books to children.While the couple's wedding attracted plenty of attention, their decision to support charitable causes before getting married gave the celebrations another dimension. Hopefully that day may not come, but I can’t control that." Head coach Shane Steichen understands the business of the NFL like Taylor, which is why he’s trying to focus on this upcoming game and the players he has on the roster. It’s hard losing Nelson, a linchpin at left guard, and Buckner, a veteran leader on the defensive line, ahead of a key divisional matchup. articles.title: Travis Kelce's $5.35 million Ohio estate faces fresh trouble as neighbors raise new objections over his security
articles.summary: Travis Kelce's return to Ohio was supposed to offer a chance to enjoy a quieter life away from the demands of professional football.
articles.body: Travis Kelce's return to Ohio was supposed to offer a chance to enjoy a quieter life away from the demands of professional football. However, settling into his new $5.35 million Bratenahl mansion has brought unexpected complications. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end is now facing resistance from people living nearby, with concerns about his property plans reaching the village's architectural review board. The latest disagreement adds another challenge to Kelce's efforts to establish a private retreat close to his hometown of Cleveland Heights.Travis Kelce's Ohio mansion becomes the center of a neighborhood disputeKelce's latest property troubles have put his new Lake Erie estate under scrutiny. Neighbors recently raised objections at a Village of Bratenahl Architectural Review Board meeting over proposed changes to the rear of the property.While the disagreement involves landscaping, the concerns extend beyond the appearance of the mansion. Residents questioned whether removing existing trees and planting new ones could affect their views of Lake Erie. They also raised concerns about possible damage to a shared sewer line that has reportedly been in place for around a century.Another sticking point was the proposed height of the replacement trees. Bratenahl's regulations set a 10-foot limit, and the original proposal did not meet that requirement.The board decided to delay its decision and requested a revised plan. Officials are expected to revisit the matter at their November 10 meeting.For Kelce, the situation creates an awkward start to life at a property that represents a major investment. The mansion is located just a few miles from Cleveland Heights, where the NFL star grew up. His connection to Ohio runs deep, making the purchase more than just another luxury real estate deal.Travis Kelce's privacy concerns add another layer to Ohio mansion dramaThe neighborhood disagreement comes after Kelce and his wife, Taylor Swift, reportedly introduced additional security measures at the property.According to Page Six, the couple installed an audible warning system designed to alert people who get too close to the estate. One neighbor described an encounter with the system to the publication.“A neighbor approached the house and got a voice warning about not passing onto the property after getting too close to the house,” another neighbor told the publication.The security arrangements have also drawn attention to privacy concerns surrounding the couple's arrival in Bratenahl. The village already has its own police force, although discussions about additional security have reportedly emerged as high-profile residents move into the area.Kelce purchased the $5.35 million estate as part of his growing property portfolio. He also owns a mansion near Kansas City, reportedly worth around $6 million, and previously bought a home in the city's Briarcliff West neighborhood.His Ohio investment gives him another place close to family and familiar surroundings. articles.title: Golden State Valkyries set ‘Super Bowl era’ record with historic WNBA championship win
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries have done something no other American sports franchise has managed after winning their first WNBA championship. Across professiona...
articles.body:
The Golden State Valkyries have done something no other American sports franchise has managed after winning their first WNBA championship.

Across professional sports in the US, expansion teams are often looked at as franchises who need time to become a serious force in their leagues. Many teams who have been added late have failed to make noticeable impacts for decades. The Golden State Valkyries have shown they do not have to be like that..

After beating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday night, the Valkyries secured their first-ever championship. Considering that this is only the second year they have existed as a team, they have officially set a mark no team has managed in the 'Super Bowl era' of professional sports in the United States.

Golden State Valkyries become the first team to win in just their second year as a franchise

In 2025, when the Valkyries joined the WNBA, they acquired most of their roster through the expansion draft. This included players like Veronica Burton and Kayla Thornton. They weren't satisfied with just what they had despite making the playoffs, adding Gabby Williams and Kiah Stokes in 2026.

Their moves and head coach Natalie Nakase's basketball savvy have resulted in the Valkyries franchise achieving something no other team has managed.

"Golden State becomes the fastest expansion team in American pro sports history (Super Bowl era) to win a title," Underdog reported. The closest any team has been to this record is the 1970-71 Milwaukee Bucks, who won in their third season. So the Valkyries have made outright history.

articles.title: 3 questions Cowboys must answer to beat the Cardinals in Week 8
articles.summary: Can Dallas change its mentality, run the ball, and put up touchdowns are questions Dallas must answer before they face the Cardinals in Week 8
articles.body:
The Cowboys beat division rival Philadelphia 38-21 to snap a two-game losing streak, and are now headed home to try for their first winning streak of the season. T he trade deadline looms and the team is deciding whether they'll be buying again. The team struggled defensively against mostly Eagles backups, but their offense stepped up with their best rushing game of the season and timely touchdown passes in the red zone. Dallas fans might have different opinions on the Cowboys' biggest rivals, but their biggest nemesis would seem to be the Arizona Cardinals .

The team is 1-8 against the Cardinals in their last nine contests, including 0-4 at AT&T Stadium, with four of their last five losses by double digits. Dallas was usually the favorite and considered the more talented team in most of those matchups, but Arizona has had their number. The Cowboys will need to answer some questions to finally get over the hump against a Cardinals team that upset the Los Angeles Rams two weeks ago.

Can Dallas continue to score touchdowns?

Dallas is seen as possibly the worst defense in the NFL, but when they match up with Arizona, it's the Cardinals who could be. They are last in scoring defense; the Cowboys are 23rd. Total yards allowed: Dallas is 29th compared to 24th for the Cardinals; EPA per play is an advantage for Arizona, 27th to 30th. They are tied at 20th in passing defense, and the Cowboys are the worst in the NFL in rushing defense.

The major difference is on the offensive side. Dallas is a top-five scoring unit and top-10 in total yards, while the Cardinals are 26th and 22nd, respectively. Both teams stink defensively and should move the ball on the other, but only one has played offense at a level to expose the other. Dallas ranks third in red-zone touchdown percentage, scoring at 74%, while Arizona ranks last at 43%.

Can Dallas continue their run game momentum?

Dallas hasn't been a good rushing team , partly due to a lack of attempts and partly to poor execution when they do hand the ball off. Going into their Week 8 breakout game in Philadelphia, they were 31st at 76 yards per game and dead last in attempts. Things improved drastically after the 200-yard rushing performance against the Philadelphia Eagles . That moved them up to 25th in the NFL with 94 yards per game.

Cowboys opponents have made it a strategy to keep the ball away from Prescott and wear down the defense, and that's why the run game is so important. The Cardinals are fourth in time of possession while the Cowboys are 29th. With Dallas' red zone advantage, if they can control the time of possession and keep their defense off the field, it could be key to a Dallas victory.

The Cowboys need a change in mentality. Confidence isn't an issue, but they have moved into the cocky category and might not even realize its impact on their play. Prescott has mentioned losing to teams they "didn't expect to lose to." Under head coach Brian Schottenheimer, the team has an under-.500 record , and hasn't beaten an NFC team outside of their own division. They shouldn't have the mentality that they should beat anybody.

The Cardinals have been the beneficiary of that mentality for multiple seasons. When Lamb was asked about the Cowboys' struggles against Arizona, he said they were "always too relaxed," and then the Cardinals would "punch them in the mouth." He went on to say they have to "treat them like they are Super Bowl contenders," but the Cowboys aren't that, so why do they play with that mentality? This thought process has to change. Stop talking about the greatest offense there is; become the team that's most prepared and plays harder than anybody else, and they'll win more games.

articles.title: Un exjugador, sobre las pérdidas de memoria por los golpes: "Recuerdo quizás hasta 2006"
articles.standfirst: Larry Johnson, que jugó en los Chiefs hasta 2009, habla de la incidencia de la encefalopatía traumática crónica (ETC), una enfermedad degenerativa asociada a los impactos
articles.summary: Larry Johnson, que jugó en los Chiefs hasta 2009, habla de la incidencia de la encefalopatía traumática crónica (ETC), una enfermedad degenerativa asociada a los impactos
articles.body: Larry Johnson, que militó gran parte de su carrera en los Kansas City Chiefs y se retiró del deporte en 2011, se ha referido recientemente a las pérdidas de memoria y las consecuencias que la encefalopatía traumática crónica (ETC), una enfermedad cerebral degenerativa asociada a repetidos impactos en la cabeza, puede haber tenido en él. A sus 46 años, Johnson asegura en una entrevista en 'The Guardian' que "recuerdo quizás hasta 2006 ó 2007. De lo anterior o de los tres años posteriores, la verdad es que no lo recuerdo". Un estudio publicado esta semana sobre exjugadores de la NFL fallecidos entre 2008 y 2023 reveló que el 74,5 % padecía CTE. De los casi 400 jugadores cuyos cerebros fueron donados para autopsia, el 93,5 % presentaba indicios de la enfermedad. Y es que esta patología sólo se puede diagnosticar cuando la persona ha fallecido. La carrera deportiva de Johnson en la NFL estuvo marcada por la exigencia física y los numerosos golpes derivado de su ímpetu en el campo. Tras la retirada, Johnson tuvo que lidiar con pensamientos intrusivos y voces internas que le decían que se hiciera daño a sí mismo y a los demás. "Hay cosas que me asustan. Ya no puedo estar cerca de los balcones. Si estoy caminando, pienso: ¿Y si algo cae del cielo ? Es un estado constante de paranoia". Para sobrellevarlo, se aisló durante largos periodos y se automedicó con drogas y alcohol, lo que empeoró aún más la situación. De hecho el exjugador sigue sufriendo episodios de confusión y a veces tiene dificultades para articular frases. Ahora su objetivo es crear una aplicación que ponga en contacto a exjugadores profesionales que tengan problemas de salud mental con personas que comprendan por lo que están pasando. Mientras, los investigadores de la encefalopatía traumática crónica siguen realizando estudios, entre ellos, ahora intentan comprobar si un fármaco aprobado por la FDA (agencia de medicamentos en USA) que reduce la inflamación también puede mejorar dichos síntomas.

articles.title: Terry Bradshaw opens up about his 'demon in the night' depression in new memoir
articles.summary: FOX Sports analyst Terry Bradshaw told Fox News about his longtime battle with depression and his latest book, “Looking for Terry: A Memoir."
articles.body: Terry Bradshaw wants men to know they aren’t alone. The FOX Sports analyst and four-time Super Bowl champion told "Fox & Friends" that "Looking for Terry: A Memoir" was a hard sell to his publisher because it isn’t about football. Instead, Bradshaw decided to open up about his longtime battle with depression. "I haven’t been public with it as much, that’s why I came out with this book," the Pittsburgh Steelers legend said during his Oct. 14 interview. TERRY BRADSHAW OPENS UP ABOUT MORTALITY AFTER BEATING CANCER TWICE: 'AM I GOING TO HEAVEN?' On the surface, Bradshaw exudes a cheerful demeanor, which he said might surprise those he opens up to about his mental health struggles. He’s had a prolific career both in the NFL and as a television sports analyst, and has built a reputation as a "tough guy." "People think, well, if you’re dealing with depression — I’m not dealing with depression right now," Bradshaw said. The Hall of Fame quarterback said depression often "rears its ugly head," but he stresses that it doesn’t rob him of his personality. Bradshaw describes it as a sickening feeling that comes over him at times and is challenging to snap out of. In "Looking for Terry," he wants readers, especially men, to be more vulnerable about their emotional struggles. Women might be more likely to get help, he said, but men often turn instead to "a few drinks and some drugs." US SOCCER LEGEND LANDON DONOVAN OPENS UP ON MENTAL HEALTH STRUGGLES, REDEFINING SUCCESS One of Bradshaw’s most challenging bouts with depression came during the 1999 Super Bowl in Miami, where he was working as a broadcaster. He told Fox News co-host Brian Kilmeade that he couldn’t get out of bed. He said his depression can emerge like a "demon in the night" during times of stress, family issues or when he is tired. Today, he has someone to lean on in his wife, Tammy. She even has a name for his depression: Roy. "She says to me, ‘Is Roy showing his ugly head?’" he explained. "I say yeah, and then we start talking about it, and I’m telling you, it’s like the greatest gift in the world just to have someone you can share that with." CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Readers of "Looking for Terry: A Memoir" will get a glimpse of an "ordinary guy who’s had an extraordinary run," not a "highlight reel," he said. Above all, Bradshaw doesn’t want people to feel sorry for him.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers’ $37K donation to New Jersey police sparks privacy backlash as critics question rich people's power over public surveillance
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers may have intended to make his former New Jersey neighbourhood safer, but his reported $37,000 contribution has sparked a much bigger debate.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers may have intended to make his former New Jersey neighbourhood safer, but his reported $37,000 contribution has sparked a much bigger debate. The NFL quarterback's donation helped fund police surveillance technology designed to track vehicles across Cedar Grove. While supporters see automatic license plate readers as useful crime-fighting tools, critics worry about who gets to decide how much surveillance a community should accept. The controversy has also raised uncomfortable questions about whether wealthy individuals can influence public security policies simply by funding them.Aaron Rodgers’ $37,000 donation funded police surveillance cameras in New JerseyRodgers reportedly made the contribution in 2024, during his time with the New York Jets. According to a FOIAball report published on August 12, 2026, the quarterback directed $37,000 towards Cedar Grove's police department to help it purchase automatic license plate reader (ALPR) cameras.The donation came through a California-based limited liability company linked to Rodgers, who reportedly served as its manager. FOIAball estimated that the amount could have covered approximately 17 cameras, giving local police additional tools to monitor vehicle movements.The town had welcomed the contribution when officials discussed the equipment at a council meeting. The town manager praised the gift, saying, “We’ve received a generous donation of new ALPR cameras … a very generous donation that the police department is receiving.”The official also highlighted the technology's value to law enforcement, adding, “These are very heavily used tools in the law enforcement toolkit, so it’s good to add more to our belt.”However, the technology has become increasingly controversial. ALPR cameras capture the licence plates of passing vehicles, allowing authorities to identify and track cars that may be connected to investigations. While this can help police locate suspects and investigate crimes, critics question how much information these systems collect and who can access it.Aaron Rodgers donation raises questions about rich people's influenceThe biggest concern surrounding the donation is not simply the presence of surveillance cameras. It is the influence private wealth can have over decisions that affect an entire community.Matthew Guariglia, a senior policy analyst at the Electronic Frontier Foundation, raised concerns about wealthy individuals funding surveillance infrastructure without broader public involvement.“This is one of just several examples nationwide now of unelected rich people getting to set the levels of surveillance in a community that they are comfortable with.”He further questioned the power that comes with such financial contributions, stating, “They get to take out their checkbook and decide how everyone in that town gets to live.”Interestingly, Rodgers has previously spoken about his own concerns regarding privacy and personal security. In December 2024, he discussed reports of mysterious drones flying over New Jersey. He also revealed in March that he had “legitimate stalkers” and had been forced to leave his Malibu home.That contrast adds another layer to the debate. While public safety remains important, residents also deserve a say in how surveillance technology operates in their neighbourhoods. The discussion now extends beyond one donation to a larger question about privacy, accountability and the role money should play in shaping public policy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles have no plans to trade running back Saquon Barkley before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have no plans to trade running back Saquon Barkley before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport .

Garafolo and Rapoport reported Sunday the Eagles "believe they still have plenty of talent on the roster to compete in 2027 and beyond." Because of that, they see a future for Barkley in Philly.

This gives the Indianapolis Colts a little more leverage with trade suitors trying to improve their backfield. Three-time Pro Bowler Jonathan Taylor is by far the best back on the market .

The Eagles are 2-5 and don't have much hope of seeing their playoff odds improve in the coming weeks. If they weren't doomed by then already, losing quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season gave them an even bigger uphill climb.

Philly traded two-time Pro Bowl lineman Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens, and many have wondered whether general manager Howie Roseman is prepared to wave the white flag and be a seller at the deadline.

Among the likely candidates, Barkley would've been one of the team's most valuable trade assets. He's only averaging 48.8 yards per game, but his 5.7 yards per carry are nearly equal to his output in 2024, when he ran for 2,005 yards.

The 29-year-old has been dogged by a hamstring injury as well.

Barkley is under contract through 2028, and his performance when healthy hasn't shown signs of falling off. If Roseman is confident in what the roster can achieve next year, then it doesn't make sense to deal the veteran ball-carrier.

That puts the spotlight even more on Indianapolis, which is in the midst of a teardown . It won't be a complete shock if Taylor is still on the Colts through the deadline. Should that happen, it won't be down to a lack of outside interest.

articles.body:
In his return from a high ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve for a month, it took just one game for Jonah Coleman to assert himself as the new lead running back in the Denver Broncos ' backfield.

As the Broncos earned a 30-16 win on the road over the Arizona Cardinals, Coleman led Denver's running back room, which also includes J.K. Dobbins and R.J. Harvey, with a 49 percent snap share. In the win, he took nine carries for 54 yards and added a pair of receptions for 15 more.

Now, with coach Sean Payton's team preparing for a matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, the former Washington Huskies star appears to be in line for a heavier workload, especially with Harvey slated to miss the game with a knee injury.

"I'm ready for any opportunity I'm given, and whenever I'm out there on the field, I'm going to give the team my all," Coleman told the media on Friday. "So I don't really control if my role is bigger or not, so just be prepared for my opportunity when I get into the game."

As Coleman has continued to pick up steam, he seems to have a strong argument to be Denver's lead back going forward after Dobbins got into a heated exchange with reporters after being asked about losing playing time to the rookie.

"I like to consider myself a pro, right? Now, if we're losing, and I'm not getting the carries, s***, I'm gonna be mad as f***," Dobbins said on Thursday. "But if we're winning, and it's working—I just want to win. I just want to win. I've been in the playoffs plenty of times. I just want to win a Super Bowl. And so, I just want to win. So, whatever it takes to do that, that's what it is."

articles.title: Ravens Discussion: Predictions for Week 8 matchup vs. Bills
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens will take on the Buffalo Bills today in a much-anticipated Week 8 contest. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s predictions for the game. Dusti...
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens will take on the Buffalo Bills today in a much-anticipated Week 8 contest. Here are Baltimore Beatdown's predictions for the game.

The Ravens have often responded with big wins in previous seasons when their backs were against the wall. That was with John Harbaugh at the helm, however, so we will have to see if Jesse Minter is able to rally the troops the same way. This game heavily hinges on how healthy Lamar Jackson is behind a shaky offensive line. If Jackson plays to the level he was performing to start the season, then Baltimore has a legitimate path to victory on Sunday. The Bills defense has struggled against the pass, so Jackson and Zay Flowers could do some real damage through the air. If Buffalo is able to get quick pressure and Jackson isn't healthy enough to evade rushers as usual, then it could be a long day for Declan Doyle. Continuing to scheme up easy plays to Flowers and letting him make plays after the catch will be needed to ease the burden on Jackson in his first game back.

X-Factor: Trenton Simpson. The Ravens defense will have their hands full with Josh Allen. Simpson has been one of the best players on Baltimore's defense to start this season, and his speed could come in handy when Allen inevitably escapes the pocket looking to make a big play through the air or as a runner. Simpson tracking down Allen on extended plays could make a huge difference if he is able to force Allen into a quicker decision with the ball.

Baltimore's secondary is already on skates heading into a matchup with Josh Allen, and Lamar Jackson is back just in time to face one of the NFL's worst passing defense. This could be a shootout of epic proportions, and it's going to come down to turnovers. The Ravens have a poor record in that regard against the Bills, but Allen isn't always careful with the ball either. Vega Ioane's absence and Jackson's still-ailing ankle will, I think, ultimately keep Baltimore's offense from making all of the plays they need to in the fourth quarter, and the defense will be inches away from the game-changing turnover that never comes. This is an opportunity for the Ravens' highest-paid defenders to step up and lead by example – can anyone deliver?

X-Factor: Nate Wiggins. Wiggins doesn't fall into the aforementioned group above, but he's extension-eligible next offseason, and he hasn't proven where he ranks among the league's corners. The key? Playmaking. He needs to use his speed not just to be sticky, but to break on passes, create turnovers, and maybe even rack up some return yardage.

There is a lot riding on this game for the Ravens. While they aren't necessarily in desperation win-now mode yet and can technically afford another loss, a victory would go a long way for both positive vibes and playoff hopes. A win over the Bills on the road could serve as a turning point for the team to turn a new page with Lamar Jackson coming back. Obviously, the Bills are going to get their share of points no matter how well the Ravens' defense can play. Josh Allen and Buffalo's offense is as dangerous as any in the NFL and they have an established offensive floor.

We've yet to see Jesse Minter's defense really dominate a game from start to finish and exceed expectations. They were just embarrassed by the Bengals last week in the second half. How will the Ravens' defense respond against another elite quarterback? This a "play for your pride" type of a spot.

X-Factor: Trey Hendrickson. The Ravens signed Hendrickson with the idea of him being the needle-moving pass rusher that can help the team close out victories. While he's been playing through a finger injury, we've yet to see Hendrickson consistently make game-changing plays and convert pressures to sacks. The Ravens could use him to come through against Allen and make a big play or two.

The Ravens are knee deep in "can't lose" territory heading up to Buffalo. The Bills, much like the Bengals, are coming off a bye and boasts the best offense in the NFL statistically. They also have one of worst defenses overall, so it looks like this will turn into a shootout.

Under different circumstances, I'd probably take the Ravens. I think the offense is capable of going shot for shot with the Bills and the Ravens defense is good enough to deliver one more stop than the Buffalo's is. However, Lamar Jackson is returning from injury and probably isn't 100%. They are going to be missing their first-round guard Vega Ioane and the Bills are coming off a bye week. So, I think the Ravens fall just short in this one. The offense will have just a couple missteps in Jackson's first game back, and the defense just won't be able to do enough to limit Josh Allen to support the offense while they get back in rhythm.

articles.title: The Bengals offensive line has been REALLY good this season
articles.summary: This is refreshing to see the Bengals’ offensive line playing the way they’re playing right now.
articles.body:
It's so interesting how when there's a problem, whether on your favorite sports team or in everyday life, you complain non-stop about it. Then when it's remedied, you don't say a peep, maybe not even acknowledging that not only is it remedied but also working really well. The Bengals' offensive line fits that exact description.

For years, Bengals fans complained about the team's offensive line. Sometimes unfairly, but the criticism was fair more often than not for the first six years of Joe Burrow's career. But over the last four years, the Bengals have quietly built what is now one of the NFL's best offensive lines.

Through six games, the Bengals have allowed just 10 sacks. And this is the heart of their success this season: Five of those sacks came in Week 2 against Houston. That means, in the other five games, Joe Burrow has only been sacked an average of one time per game. One time per game. That's it.

It's been four years since the Bengals were in the Playoffs. The last time they played a playoff game was in the AFC Championship Game in January of 2023. They did so with three backup offensive linemen taking the field that night at Arrowhead Stadium. That night, the Bengals gained zero yards in the first quarter, and Joe Burrow was sacked on the Bengals' final offensive play of the game.

Less than two months later, the Bengals swung big and signed the best left tackle in free agency in Orlando Brown Jr.. Brown has signed multiple contract extensions with the Bengals since then. After Week 2, there was concern about him, and rightfully so. He had a rough preseason and training camp.

But since Week 2 against Houston, have you even noticed him? It was worth keeping your stock in him.

With the 18th pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, the Bengals drafted Amarius Mims out of Georgia. There was concern over his limited playing time in college, but that's not at all the conversation now about the Bengals' franchise right tackle. He looks like the second coming of Willie Anderson.

Watch the play where Burrow stepped up in the pocket and found Tee Higgins for a 44-yard gain Sunday. At the outset of the play, Mims erased Ravens edge rusher Mike Green completely out of the play. It was impressive.

How about the interior of the Bengals' offensive line? Ted Karras is the only starter from the Bengals' offensive line from that 2022 AFC Championship still with the team. He's as solid as they come and a true leader on this team. Dylan Fairchild is unnoticeable at left guard.

Yes, he's had a couple of key holding penalties this season, but he's playing really well in his second season. He looks like a home run who the Bengals drafted in the third round of the 2025 Draft. Dalton Risner signed with the Bengals last August, just a week before the season started. He's blocking incredibly well both in the passing and running games. Since becoming the full-time starter at right guard in the middle of last season, the Bengals' offense has been much more fluid upfront.

In the second half Sunday, Joe Burrow had clean pockets every time he dropped back to pass. When was the last time you saw the Bengals control the line of scrimmage like that, especially in a division game?

The Bengals finally have a really good offensive line in front of Joe Burrow. They deserve their credit, even if they want to go through life anonymously. Fans complained about the Bengals' offensive line for years and, more often than not, rightfully so. But now, fans aren't talking about the Bengals' offensive line even though they deserve a lot of credit. That's a good thing. Still, though, the Bengals' offensive line is playing really good football heading into November.

articles.title: New Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors on Christian McCaffrey Value Eyed by Colts and Irsay-Gordon Meeting
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are using the 2022 Christian McCaffrey trade as a general baseline for any deal involving star running back Jonathan Taylor, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are using the 2022 Christian McCaffrey trade as a general baseline for any deal involving star running back Jonathan Taylor, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Schefter reported Sunday the Colts "would seek a similar compensation package" to what the Carolina Panthers received. The San Francisco 49ers gave up second-, third- and fourth-round picks in the 2023 NFL draft and a 2024 fifth-rounder.

Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Saturday that Taylor and Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon had "an in-depth conversation" to go over his situation.

"Irsay-Gordon is said to have an affinity for the three-time Pro Bowler, and the Colts would prefer for Taylor to be a part of their rebuild," per the report.

"The list of teams that have expressed at least some level of interest in trading for Taylor is thought to include the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings and New York Giants, sources said," per Schefter.

Rapoport and colleague Mike Garafolo reported Sunday the Philadelphia Eagles aren't moving Saquon Barkley ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. For teams in need of running back help, Taylor is by far the biggest piece on the board.

That might aid in Indy's efforts to extract as much value as possible.

A McCaffrey-like haul could be attainable when the four-time Pro Bowler was only one year younger at the time of his trade to the Niners. He had also appeared in just 10 games between 2020 and 2021, so his stock had dipped a bit because of injury concerns.

Taylor is a different kind of backfield threat, though. He's not the pass-catcher McCaffrey is, and that could influence how front offices evaluate him.

Taylor's production on the ground does speak for itself. He's averaging 83.9 rushing yards per game, and his career average (89.9) ranks fifth all time.

The two-year, $44 million extension he signed with the Colts could be viewed favorably, too. He'll be a free agent in 2029, his age-30 season. Any team acquiring him will have some cost certainty for the next few years without being committed to a point where his performance could begin to decline.

All things considered, you'd probably expect Taylor to be wearing a different jersey within a few weeks given the Colts' ongoing reset. They might be perfectly happy to keep him in the fold as an offensive building block in 2027.

articles.title: Bears' Caleb Williams Reportedly 'Refusing to Cover' Logo on Custom Cleats Despite NFL Warning, Fine
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is "refusing to cover up the logo" on his Caddix cleats, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is "refusing to cover up the logo" on his Caddix cleats, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Rapoport described it as "a matter of principle more than anything."

Caddix isn't an approved apparel provider for the NFL. In cases like this, a player has to cover the company logo when wearing the gear during games.

Williams isn't an endorser of Caddix but came to prefer that cleat. Company CEO Jack Rasmussen is capitalizing on the situation and pledged to pay whatever fines Williams receives from the league:

Rapoport drew a comparison to a similar situation with former Bears quarterback Jim McMahon. McMahon drew the ire of the league office for donning an Adidas headband and eventually wrote the name of commissioner Pete Rozelle on the accessory.

Caddix likely isn't a name familiar to a lot of fans. Rasmussen told Rapoport that Williams wanted to give the footwear a try, and things took off from there.

"His QB trainer called us last year and said Caleb was interested in trying them," Rasmussen said. "We talked for months about the cleats and trying different models, so I flew down to Jacksonville, met Caleb, made him show me what he wanted in a cleat and figured out what he needed. It took us two more iterations to find one he liked."

Williams is collecting $4.4 million in NFL salary for 2026 on top of whatever he's making off the field. Collective fines of $35,823 are a drop in the bucket.

And for Rasmussen, picking up the tab is a bargain for how much publicity Caddix is receiving.

articles.title: New Breece Hall Trade Rumors on Jets' Stance amid Braelon Allen's Emergence Ahead of NFL Deadline
articles.summary: A trade involving New York Jets running back Breece Hall "seems unlikely," according to ESPN's Rich Cimini.
articles.body:
A trade involving New York Jets running back Breece Hall "seems unlikely," according to ESPN's Rich Cimini .

Braelon Allen has run for 357 yards and one touchdown over the past four weeks, leading some fans to wonder whether New York trading Hall is a possibility.

Cimini reported the team is happy to keep both Allen and Hall: "The Jets believe that they have the NFL's best 1-2 punch, and they don't want to break it up. Even if they wanted to move him, Hall's recent injuries may give teams pause. He has missed four games because of a quadriceps injury after missing a chunk of training camp because of a strained groin."

The Jets wouldn't be selling high on Hall if they decided on this course of action. In addition to his injuries, the 25-year-old combined to run for 61 yards in the two weeks after his 102-yard showing in a 23-10 win over the Tennessee Titans.

Given the state of the passing game, having Hall and Allen together in 2027 would provide a solid foundation for the offense.

Geno Smith is a stopgap under center, and it feels inevitable that the Jets will invest valuable draft capital in the quarterback position next spring. Miami's Darian Mensah was the pick in Bleacher Report's most recent mock .

Being able to pose a consistent threat on the ground will ease some of the pressure on the heir apparent, whoever it is.

Not to mention, the general excitement around Allen is based around a small sample. He had 410 combined rushing yards through his first two seasons in the league.

One risk to trading Hall is that Allen could regress in the second half, thus lowering the confidence level in the latter as a No. 1 option on his own.

Maybe a rival team loves Hall enough to table a massive offer, one New York can't turn down. Absent that, moving him shouldn't merit a lot of consideration.

articles.title: East Carolina Pirates' David Coleman Jr suffers fractured leg after slip by referee
articles.summary: A referee accidentally fractures a college football player's leg during a bizarre incident in the first half of East Carolina Pirates' win against Temple Owls.
articles.body:
A referee accidentally fractured a college football player's leg during a bizarre incident in the first half of East Carolina Pirates' win against Temple Owls.

East Carolina defensive back David Coleman Jr was standing on the field with team-mates in between plays, when an official ran in to address something near the 40-yard line.

As the official approached the players from behind, he slipped and slid into Coleman Jr, who fell forward to the ground.

Coleman Jr stayed on the turf, before eventually being helped from the field by two team members, who carried him so he did not have to put weight on his injured leg.

East Carolina coach Blake Harrell later confirmed Coleman Jr had an X-ray at half-time which showed he fractured his fibula during the incident.

"Our thoughts and our prayers are with him. But that's just one of those things. Kind of wild it happens, I'd never seen that from an official," said Blake.

East Carolina won the game 17-9, with Coleman Jr recording one tackle during the match before he left the field.

The Hall of Famer was also a master motivator as a player, and that hasn't changed after he retired. Here's one such example from when he tried to fire up the locker room following a 1-6 start to the 2015 season.

articles.title: How Myles Garrett Impacted Jeffery Simmons' Trade to Bears from Titans Revealed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns' decision to trade star pass-rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams this past offseason reportedly set off a process that ended with the Chicago Bears acquiring defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns' decision to trade star pass-rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams this past offseason reportedly set off a process that ended with the Chicago Bears acquiring defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday that Bears general manager Ryan Poles and Titans general manager Mike Borgonzi used the Garrett trade as the blueprint to complete the move that sent Simmons to the Windy City.

Los Angeles traded a 2027 first-round draft pick, a 2028 second-round pick, a 2029 third-round pick and pass-rusher Jared Verse for Garrett.

"The Titans viewed Verse as the equivalent of a first-round pick for comparative purposes, and that Garrett deal formed the framework for the trade that sent Simmons to Chicago with a 2028 fifth-round pick in exchange for two first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-round pick," Schefter explained.

Fox Sports' Jay Glazer reported Sunday that Poles differentiated himself from other suitors in the discussions by immediately offering multiple first-round picks:

Poles and Borgonzi previously worked together with the Kansas City Chiefs, so there was already a relationship in place.

It was a trade that underscored the difference between the two franchises in 2026.

The Bears are in win-now mode with a franchise quarterback in place with Caleb Williams and a defense that needed improvement if they are going to keep pace with the best teams in the NFC come playoff time.

Schefter reported Poles and Co. "studied every Super Bowl champion since 2018 and noticed that each one had an elite defensive tackle" with players such as Aaron Donald, Chris Jones, Vita Vea, Fletcher Cox, Jalen Carter and Leonard Williams all lifting the Lombardi Trophy.

As for the 1-6 Titans who are also coming off back-to-back 3-14 seasons, they are in full-on rebuilding mode and need draft capital with an eye toward the future.

According to Schefter, the AFC South team looked at the draft capital that came back in previous blockbuster deals when deciding to move Simmons.

For example, the Detroit Lions used picks they got for Matthew Stafford to end up with Jahmyr Gibbs, Sam LaPorta and Jameson Williams, while the Browns eventually got Mason Graham, Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson and KC Concepcion after trading the No. 2 pick of the 2025 draft to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The end result was the Titans landing multiple first-rounders they could eventually use to help build their next contending roster and the Bears landing one of the best defensive tackles in the league as they attempt to take the next step after reaching the Divisional Round last season.

It will likely take multiple years to see the full impact of the trade, but there was reportedly plenty of research that went into the move on both sides. And some of that research included using the Garrett move from earlier this year to guide the way.

articles.title: Packers' interest in Jonathan Taylor shows desire to move on from Josh Jacobs and his domestic abuse issues
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers' pursuit of Jonathan Taylor a sign Josh Jacobs' days in Green Bay seem numbered amid expanding domestic abuse allegations.
articles.body: Jonathan Taylor's almost certain trade from the Indianapolis Colts by the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline comes with a multitude of subplots but none more gripping than the interest the Green Bay Packers have in the running back and what that means. The Packers' interest, at whatever level that has reached, shows the team's willingness to move on from Pro Bowl running back Josh Jacobs, who is currently on their roster but has been a disappointment and something of a headaches because of his legal problems. It has been widely reported, and confirmed by OutKick and Fox News Digital that the Packers are among the teams that have expressed varying degrees of interest in trading for Taylor – a list that includes the Denver Broncos, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants and, yes, the Packers. PACKERS ACTIVATE JOSH JACOBS; RUNNING BACK SET TO PLAY IN FIRST GAME SINCE DOMESTIC VIOLENCE ARREST And while the interest from the other teams is generally tied to a desire get consistent production in their running game, the Packers' interest glows in neon because Jacobs' days with the Packers seem numbered. Jacobs, 28, has played in two games for Green Bay this season after spending the first six games on the Commissioner’s Exempt List — which is effectively a paid suspension. That time on the list followed Jacobs pleading no contest in September to battery and criminal-damage-to-property charges stemming from a May domestic incident with his former girlfriend. But Jacobs remains under serious NFL scrutiny as the league said Saturday it is reviewing previously unreported allegations that Jacobs physically abused three other women. Duchac III, released a statement Saturday addressing the allegations by saying police had weighed the allegations from the three other women and moved forward with "only two misdemeanor charges." articles.title: Jordyn Tyson Injury Update, Latest Rumors and Timeline for Saints WR to Make NFL Debut
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson is reportedly getting closer to making his NFL debut.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson is reportedly getting closer to making his NFL debut.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Tyson could return from his hamstring injury as early as the team's Week 9 matchup with the Cleveland Browns. Even if he ultimately can't suit up against Cleveland, he's "not far away from playing."

The No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft has spent the Saints' first seven games of the year on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury that he suffered during a joint practice with the Jacksonville Jaguars on Aug. 13.

It was a tough blow to New Orleans' receiving corps, as Tyson was reportedly turning heads in training camp.

The 22-year-old previously dealt with health issues throughout his college career, missing time due to a knee injury in 2022 before a collarbone injury impacted his 2024 campaign.

In 2025, Tyson was limited to nine games with a hamstring injury that also prevented him from participating in the scouting combine.

Still, his productivity when available resulted in the Saints selecting him with their first choice in the draft.

Tyson wrapped up a 2025 season at Arizona State in which he hauled in 61 receptions for 711 yards and eight touchdowns. He also racked up 1,101 yards and 10 scores during the prior year, averaging 14.7 yards per reception.

The Saints have opened their 2026 campaign with a 2-5 record, which includes losses in four of their past five games. Chris Olave has continued to serve as New Orleans' No. 1 receiver, catching 49 passes for 636 yards and two touchdowns.

The Saints currently have a Week 8 bye, giving Tyson additional time to recover before potentially returning to the field against the Browns on Nov. 8.

articles.title: Jauan Jennings Snubs 49ers Trade, New NFL Rumors Reveal on Vikings WR Ahead of 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings declined to reunite with the San Francisco 49ers on the trade market, according to Fox Sports' Jay Glazer.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings declined to reunite with the San Francisco 49ers on the trade market, according to Fox Sports' Jay Glazer.

"The 49ers, who already traded for DeForest Buckner, also had trade terms worked out for Jauan Jennings, their former receiver with the Vikings," Glazer reported Sunday (0:48 mark). "But it was contingent upon him hopping on a FaceTime with Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch and saying, 'Okay, yeah. I want to come back.' But he didn't. He said, 'Actually, no. I want to stay here in Minnesota.'"

Jennings is in the midst of his inaugural season on the Vikings after spending the first five years of his career in San Francisco.

Minnesota owns the best record in the NFL at 6-0 this season, although the 49ers aren't far behind at 6-1.

The Vikings' strong start has been primarily fueled by their defense, as they own the league's fourth-worst passing attack by averaging a mere 162.3 yards per game through the air.

Jennings has caught four of his eight targets for 43 yards across five appearances this year.

Meanwhile, San Francisco boasts the NFL's No. 10 passing offense .

49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has put together an impressive 2026 campaign, completing 69.2 percent of his throws for 1,748 yards and 15 touchdowns compared to four interceptions.

Jennings is familiar with catching passes from Purdy, as he hauled in a career-high 77 receptions for 975 yards during the 2024 season.

The receiver went through a contract dispute with the 49ers near the end of the ensuing offseason, though.

Jennings eventually stayed on the team and amassed 643 yards the following year, but San Francisco let him depart in free agency.

The 29-year-old may have had an opportunity for a larger role by coming back to the 49ers this season, but he doesn't seem to be interested in playing for his former team.

articles.body:
Former New York Jets coach Rex Ryan had choice words for Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty as the teams prepared to play Sunday.

Jeanty drew the ire of Ryan after telling reporters the Jets have some defensive players "that don't really want to tackle."

Ryan responded by calling the second-year back "soft as Charmin" and asserting he's "about the worst draft pick in the last 20 years":

Jeanty put a big target on his back with how he dismissed the Jets defense, and he displayed a level of confidence he may not have earned on the field.

Calling the former Boise State star the worst pick from the last 20 years is a stretch, but his production so far has been underwhelming to say the least.

Through 24 games, Jeanty has run for 1,303 yards and six touchdowns, and he's averaging just 3.5 yards per carry. In the Week 7 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, he had 15 yards on the ground.

Challenging the Jets defense so openly is bound to generate a response as well.

New York hasn't been great against the run. The team is surrendering 127.7 yards per game, good for 24th in the league.

It's not as simple as the Jets flipping a switch and becoming an elite defensive team, but you can rest assured they'll give Jeanty and the Raiders offense their best shot.

articles.title: Russell Wilson Video Picking Broncos-Chiefs Goes Viral After Sean Payton Saga
articles.summary: Russell Wilson and Sean Payton probably aren't going to be hanging out anytime soon, but the retired quarterback still feels his former head coach is going to get the win Sunday.
articles.body:
Russell Wilson and Sean Payton probably aren't going to be hanging out anytime soon, but the retired quarterback still feels his former head coach is going to get the win Sunday.

"Sean Payton you may like me, you may not but I'm picking you," Wilson said Sunday as part of CBS' pregame coverage ahead of the game between Payton's Denver Broncos and the Kansas City Chiefs.

Wilson played for Payton's Broncos during the 2023 season, although he did return the following year when Denver decided to release him and still pay the remainder of his salary.

As ESPN's Jordan Raanan noted in 2025, Payton benched Wilson during that 2023 campaign they were together in Denver. He then released the 10-time Pro Bowler even though there was still a head-turning $85 million in dead money remaining on the signal-caller's contract.

"The relationship between coach and quarterback had soured," Raanan wrote at the time while discussing comments Payton made regarding a 2025 meeting between the Broncos and New York Giants. "It does not appear to have been repaired."

Wilson was on the Giants at the time, but the NFC East team decided to make the switch to Jaxson Dart during the season.

"They found a little spark with that quarterback. I was talking to John Mara not too long ago and I said we were hoping that change would've happened long after our game," Payton said.

That remark drew quite the response from Wilson, who even mentioned the Bountygate scandal that ended in Payton's suspension for the 2012 season:

Wilson discussed his social media post in March during an appearance on the Bussin' With The Boys podcast (h/t Grant Gordon of NFL.com) and said, "I know who I am as a competitor, as a warrior, as a champion, too and you know, I've beaten Sean, too. You know, like we've been on the same place and the same thing. And so, it's not a matter of disrespect. Just don't disrespect me."

Payton and Wilson may not be best friends, but the coach can at least take solace knowing the quarterback-turned-analyst believes his team will pick up a key win on Sunday.

Kansas City is in first place in the AFC West at 5-1 and just ahead of the 5-2 Broncos. The winner will be in first place near the halfway mark of the season and have an important divisional victory as well.

articles.title: Jessie Bates’ forced touchback is one of NFL’s best defensive plays this year in Falcons-Bucs
articles.summary: Jessie Bates made one of the best defensive plays of the NFL season to save a touchdown.
articles.body:
Jessie Bates is widely considered one of the best safeties in the NFL. The Atlanta Falcons star is particularly good at forcing takeaways, and he just proved it again during one of the wildest plays of the season so far in his team's Week 8 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Bucs QB Baker Mayfield fumbled the snap, picked up the ball, started to scramble, then lateraled it to running back Bucky Irving in what looked like a college football option play. Irving was making his way to an open end zone when Bates came in with his signature Peanut Punch to knock the ball free inside of the one-yard-line and out of the end zone for a touchdown.

Talk about a game-breaking play. Watch Bates' forced fumble here:

That should have been six points for the Bucs. Instead, Bates made a heroic play to jar the ball loose, and it bounced perfectly in Atlanta's favor to result in a touchback.

Every team in the NFC South entered the week under .500. It's been a rough start to the season for both Tampa and Atlanta, but there's always an opportunity in the worst division in football, and it's creating games that are way more intense than they have any right to be.

Bates is a stud. The Falcons are lucky to have him.

articles.title: "Well, it's prostate cancer": George Kittle opens up about cancer's impact on his family and how the experience changed him forever
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle wants men to pay closer attention to their health, a message shaped by a personal family experience.
articles.body: San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle wants men to pay closer attention to their health, a message shaped by a personal family experience. His grandfather was diagnosed with prostate cancer around a decade ago, but Kittle admits he initially knew very little about the disease or his family's medical history. His grandfather died of natural causes last year. That loss prompted Kittle to speak with his father, Bruce, about their family's health risks and reconsider how seriously he should take his own health. He is now using his platform to encourage men to get checked.George Kittle's grandfather's cancer diagnosis changed his outlookGeorge Kittle's grandfather received his prostate cancer diagnosis roughly 10 years ago. However, the seven-time Pro Bowl tight end did not fully understand what the diagnosis meant at the time. He had little knowledge of prostate cancer and had never paid much attention to the family's medical history.Speaking to People, Kittle recalled his initial reaction to learning about the disease."I had zero awareness. I had no idea about anything except I was just like, all right, well it's prostate cancer. I don't know anything," Kittle told People.His grandfather's death last year gave him another reason to understand the family's medical background. Kittle sat down with his father, Bruce, to discuss their health history and learn what he might need to watch for in the future.That conversation also changed his approach to preventive care. Rather than treating medical checks as something to consider only when a problem appears, Kittle wants men to understand the value of knowing their risks early.He has since partnered with Novartis as an ambassador and taken part in its "Relax, It's a Blood Test" campaign. The initiative, which featured several NFL players earlier this year, aims to make conversations about prostate cancer screening less uncomfortable for men.George Kittle urges men not to delay prostate cancer screeningGeorge Kittle's message comes against the backdrop of prostate cancer's impact on men's health in the United States. Excluding skin cancer, it is the most commonly diagnosed cancer among American men. The American Cancer Society estimates that about one in eight men will develop the disease during their lifetime.Early detection can make a significant difference. Novartis reports that the five-year relative survival rate for prostate cancer exceeds 99% when the disease is caught early.Kittle believes men should not overthink the first step. Speaking about the screening process, he explained how a simple conversation with a doctor can help someone understand what comes next."You go in, get blood tested and then you continue to live your life," Kittle told People. "It's not scary, it's not intimidating, it's pretty straightforward."He also offered a blunt reminder to men who might be avoiding the appointment."Relax. It's a blood test. It's so easy. Trust me, I get IVs, I get blood tests, I get acupuncture. You can deal with the needle," Kittle said.He was careful not to present himself as a medical expert, adding, "I'm not a doctor, but you should talk to your doctor."The message carries added weight after Kittle's own difficult year. He tore his Achilles during the playoffs in January and returned to the field last month after rehabilitation. He credited his approach to setbacks for helping him through the recovery."I try to attack everything with a violently positive mindset," he told People. "It doesn't matter your situation, just attack it as best you can."His wife, Claire, his parents and the medical professionals involved in his rehabilitation also played an important role. Their support helped him maintain that outlook during a challenging recovery.For Kittle, the conversation about health now extends beyond football. His grandfather's experience made him ask questions he had never thought to raise before. He wants other men to do the same, starting with a conversation they might otherwise keep postponing.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson ruled out after hurting thumb on right throwing hand
articles.summary: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has been ruled out after hurting the thumb on his right throwing hand on Baltimore’s first offensive snap against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.
articles.body: ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has been ruled out after hurting the thumb on his right throwing hand on Baltimore’s first offensive snap against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. Jackson was hurt in his first start after missing three games with an ankle injury, and while dropping back and bouncing a pass attempt to Zay Flowers. Jackson was unable to finish his follow-through as his right hand struck pass rusher Greg Rousseau’s arm. Jackson immediately began heading off the field and appeared to point to his thumb before taking a knee before reaching the sideline. He was immediately escorted up the tunnel with backup Tyler Huntley taking over. After initially listing Jackson as questionable, the Ravens listed him as out before the first quarter ended. Baltimore (4-3) went 1-2 in Jackson’s absence in a stretch in which the Ravens offensive production drastically dropped off under Huntley. Baltimore scored 63 fewer points and averaged 3 fewer yards per play in the past three games as opposed to the first three under Jackson.
